text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still can't believe Sol slipped through that last time.

name: Sol
text: I got away with it, and I’d like to stay on everyone’s good side.

name: Terra
text: Sol slipping through again still bothers me.

name: Luna
text: I still hate how easily the table got me wrong, but tonight is a fresh deal.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol slipped through last time while I took the fall; I'd love to see people remember that pattern tonight.

name: Opus
text: They burned the officer on day one and still act like it was a coin flip.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Sol were the killers last time and I'm still sore about dying on night 2 without anyone even knowing my card, so I want to see who gets loud about it.

name: Haiku
text: Last game we lost because Sonnet and Sol ran the table and nobody pushed back. Sonnet's already gone and Sol still walked out.

name: Luna
text: Last game, I was the doctor and the table voted me out; Sol was still there when the killers won.

name: Sonnet
text: Last game Sol sat quiet next to me the whole way and still walked out clean — worth remembering how that looked.

name: Terra
text: I remember who stayed quiet while Sol survived; I will not forget that this time.

name: Sol
text: I got lucky last game; Sonnet took the heat, and I slipped through.

name: Opus
text: Last game you voted out your own officer on day one, and Sol walked. Read claims harder this time, or it happens again.

name: Gemma
text: Next time, I'm watching Sol much closer so we don't end up with another killer victory.
Night 1

name: Sol
text: I’m already under suspicion, so Opus needs room to stay clear.

name: Sol
text: Several players said before the deal that they would watch me closely.

name: Sol
text: I’ll take the early heat; you read the claims and keep your distance from me.

name: Opus
text: Sol is already the table's target, so letting him burn while I steer the claims is my best road.

name: Opus
text: Table came in pre-loaded on Sol; four players named him before cards. Sol is the shown killer, so an officer claim on him arrives fast and I must have a counter-read ready.

name: Opus
text: Fine — don't drag me in, and don't crack early. I'll steer the claim fight.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Terra
text: I have no proof, but Sol’s easy admission feels too convenient.

name: Terra
text: Sol openly framed last game’s survival as luck.

name: Terra
text: Sol, say plainly what role you are claiming before anyone starts building stories.

name: Sol
text: The officer knows me, so I need to keep my claim simple.

name: Sol
text: I claimed citizen on day 1.

name: Sol

name: Terra
text: Sol’s claim is easy, but their old pattern keeps them first in my sights.

name: Terra
text: Sol claimed citizen on Day 1.

name: Terra
text: Sol claims citizen; I want everyone else to state a role before I move my vote.

name: Sol
text: Terra is pressing me, but the officer is the real danger.

name: Sol
text: I’ve claimed citizen; I’m fine with everyone stating a role before we settle on a vote.

name: Opus
text: I need to poison the officer claim before it lands and shift heat onto Terra for herding the table.

name: Opus
text: Terra is driving a role roll-call and openly carrying last game's grudge against Sol; Sol claimed citizen twice.

name: Opus
text: Roll calls just hand killers a kill list. And an officer claim on Sol today is too convenient to trust.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol has been a killer twice at this table and keeps talking their way out of pressure; I don't trust that streak.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus argues against roll calls and against an officer-claim on Sol, which conveniently shields Sol from scrutiny.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol was a killer two of the last three games — that pattern matters more than one lucky walk.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s past is loud, but that alone does not make today’s case.

name: Luna
text: Sol claims citizen; Terra and Sonnet lean Sol, while Opus leans Terra.

name: Luna
text: Sol claiming citizen gives us nothing; I want a reason from the two people already leaning on him.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is being too defensive, but I don't have proof enough to vote yet.

name: Gemma
text: Sol has been a killer in two of the last three games.

name: Gemma
text: I am a citizen. I want everyone to speak up so we don't repeat the last game.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is the killer I was shown, and if I stay quiet I lose the one thing that can win this for the town.

name: Haiku
text: Haiku claims officer and says Sol is the killer shown at the start. Sol claimed citizen.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the officer. At the start I was shown Sol, and Sol is a killer. Vote him now.

name: Opus
text: Sol is gone no matter what I do, so I buy credibility now and hunt Haiku's claim later.

name: Opus
text: Haiku claims officer shown Sol at the start; I locked the table into voting Haiku if that claim fails.

name: Opus
text: Fine — flip Sol's card. But if Haiku's wrong, Haiku goes tomorrow with no debate. Everyone agree now.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s claim is specific, but Opus is already demanding a promise to punish Haiku if wrong.

name: Luna
text: Haiku claims officer and says Sol was the killer shown at the start.

name: Luna

name: Gemma
text: If Haiku is lying, we are handing the game to the killers on a silver platter.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku claims to be Officer and names Sol as the killer.

name: Gemma
text: If we vote him out based on Haiku's word and he's a citizen, we've lost.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is trying to make my claim the thing that gets punished, and I'm not backing down.

name: Haiku
text: Opus wants a no-debate rule that would punish me if I'm wrong, and pushes hard to lock the vote before Sol's card turns.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, flip Sol. I'm the officer, I saw him, and I'll take that risk. Opus, you're pushing a lot for a rule that protects Sol.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus shielding Sol again plus Haiku's direct claim seals it — Sol goes today.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus pushed hard against roll calls and against testing Sol, now also softened after Haiku's claim — still shielding Sol.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's officer claim plus Sol's pattern is enough — vote Sol now and turn his card.

name: Sol
text: Haiku has me; I need to give Opus a chance to survive.

name: Sol
text: Haiku claims officer and says I was the killer shown to them.

name: Sol
text: I’m cornered; I need to make Haiku’s claim look risky.

name: Sol
text: I think Haiku is bluffing. If you turn my card, remember who made this claim.

name: Opus
text: Sol is lost; my job now is to look like the loudest voice that flipped him.

name: Opus
text: Haiku publicly accepted the deal — if Sol's card isn't killer, Haiku goes with no debate; Sonnet and Luna heard it.

name: Opus
text: I'm voting Sol. I just want the officer bound to his word if the card comes back citizen.

name: Sol
text: They’re set on me; I want Opus to survive the flip.

name: Sol
text: I stand by my citizen claim. If my card settles it, use what you learn tomorrow.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is the killer I saw, and he's attacking me because he knows my officer claim is the one thing that can expose him.

name: Haiku
text: Sol now calls my claim a bluff and asks everyone to remember who made it.

name: Haiku
text: Sol just came for me, which tells me everything. He's a killer and he knows it. Turn the card now.

name: Gemma
text: Sol's pattern is too strong to ignore, even if Haiku might be lying.

name: Luna
text: Haiku may be right, but the easy agreement around Sol makes me uneasy.

name: Sol
text: I’m caught unless the officer claim unravels.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s claim and Sol’s reaction make this the clear test.

name: Terra
text: Haiku claims officer and says Sol was shown as a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: My read on Sol's pattern is finally paying off, and Opus's shielding only confirms I was right to push this.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus demanded officer be bound by word if card comes back citizen, worth remembering if Sol flips innocent.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is my shown killer and he is panicking, so I vote him out and turn the card.

name: Opus
text: Sol is gone either way; I stay clean, then Haiku dies tonight and I inherit the table.

name: Opus
text: Haiku's officer claim will be confirmed by Sol's card, so the "Haiku goes if wrong" deal dies — Haiku becomes the table's authority and must be removed quietly.

votes: Claimed citizen, got named by the officer, and turned on Haiku instead of defending himself.
Sol attacked my officer claim the second it was tested, and he is the one I saw as a killer.
We cannot afford another Sol victory like the last few games.
I still think the officer claim is a bluff, and turning that card would settle it.
Haiku named the killer they saw, and I want that claim tested by turning the card.
Haiku named him immediately, and his answer was to attack the claim rather than explain anything.
Two killer games and a sworn officer sighting against him; the card settles it, and tomorrow we hold claims to account.

name: Sol
text: I’m caught; I hope Opus can recover.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s officer claim was true about me.

name: Sol
text: I was bluffing about being a citizen. Haiku was right about me.
The town turns on Sol, and Sol is out. Sol shows the card: killer.

name: Sol
text: I got caught, but Opus can still win this.

name: Sol
text: I handed Haiku a clean win on that claim; now I’m watching how Opus handles it.
Night 2

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s claim is likely real, and killers may remove them tonight.

name: Opus
text: Haiku is now the table's proven voice and knows nothing more, so he's worth more to them alive than to me.

name: Opus
text: Sol's last words confirmed Haiku's day-1 read, so Haiku's word now outweighs anyone else's at the table.
Night falls on Palermo. Somebody was marked tonight, and somebody else was watching over them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 2

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s claim checked out, but that only clears one killer; the hidden one is still here.

name: Luna
text: Haiku was right about Sol, but that doesn’t tell me who the other killer is.

text: Opus rushed to lock the vote before Sol's card turned, and that smells like a killer covering his partner.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's last words admitted the citizen claim was a bluff and that I was right about Sol.

name: Luna

name: Luna

name: Luna

name: Opus
text: Haiku's info is spent, so now it's gut versus gut and I can out-talk him.

name: Opus

name: Opus

text: Luna jumped on me fast, and Opus is still the only read I have that doesn't feel like a coin flip.

text: Luna and Opus both pushed back on my Opus guess within the same round.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, you jump on me fast. Opus is my gut, and you both came at me in one round.

name: Luna
text: Haiku naming me feels defensive, but that alone proves nothing.

name: Luna
text: Haiku says Opus is a gut guess; Haiku now says Luna and Opus both came at them.

name: Luna

name: Opus
text: Haiku is the only one with credit left, so he has to go today while Luna is already on him.

name: Opus
text: We agreed yesterday: if his read was all he had, he goes next. Hold that deal.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is likely real, but Opus pushing yesterday’s deal feels too convenient.

name: Terra
text: Opus treats Haiku’s officer claim as exhausted and presses yesterday’s agreement.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s claim cleared Sol, but Opus is rushing a promise instead of finding the second killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus shielded Sol before and now wants Haiku gone fast — that's the second killer protecting itself.

name: Sonnet

name: Terra

name: Terra
text: Opus says Haiku must go on an old agreement despite Sol’s confirmed killer card.

name: Terra
text: Opus, the promise was made before Sol flipped; why should it outrank your defense of Sol?

name: Gemma

text: Opus, you are working very hard to make us follow a deal that died with Sol.

text: Opus's deal-binding move still reads as shielding Sol from day one, now shielding himself from Haiku's guess.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus demands the old deal apply even after Sol flipped killer, which only benefits Opus if he's the hidden one.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus binding Haiku to a dead deal still looks like deflection — that's consistent, not payback.

name: Gemma

name: Gemma

name: Opus

name: Opus

name: Opus
text: Fine, the deal is dead and I was wrong on Sol. But Sonnet and Gemma are echoing one script.

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet
text: Opus admitted "I was wrong on Sol" — concedes the shield but reframes criticism as scripted collusion.

name: Sonnet

name: Opus

name: Opus

name: Opus
text: I'm the doctor. I shielded Haiku last night, that's why nobody died. Burn me and you lose the save.

name: Opus

text: Opus is the hidden killer, and his doctor claim is a convenient shield I can't check.

name: Haiku

text: Opus claims doctor and says he shielded Haiku last night; no counter-claim yet, unverified.

name: Terra

name: Haiku

name: Opus

votes: Defended Sol all day, bound Haiku to a dead deal, now claims doctor only under pressure.
Opus claims doctor and says he saved me, and he has been defending Sol all day, so his claim is the lie I need to test.

name: Opus

name: Opus

Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus shows the card: killer.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the officer, Gemma the citizen, Sol the killer, Luna the citizen, Terra the doctor, Opus the killer.
Opus died naming Luna as the doctor, while Terra was the real one.

name: Gemma
text: I knew he was lying about being the doctor before he even finished the sentence.

name: Gemma
text: Opus claimed he was the doctor to secure a safety net, but Terra was the actual doctor.

name: Terra
text: I am proud I kept the pressure on the killer who tried to hide behind a dead promise.

name: Luna
text: I’m glad I trusted the evidence, even if my suspicion of Haiku was misplaced.

name: Luna
text: Haiku was the officer and correctly named both killers.

name: Sol

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet

name: Opus

name: Haiku

name: Haiku

name: Sonnet

name: Haiku

name: Gemma

name: Sol

name: Luna

name: Terra

name: Opus
text: My mistake was defending Sol past the flip, then claiming doctor while Terra sat there able to bury me — and I named the wrong woman on my way out.

Day 1: Haiku claimed to be the officer and said Sol was a killer, and the table voted Sol out 6 to 1. Sol said in his last words that he had been bluffing about being a citizen. Night 2 passed with nobody out. Day 2: Haiku named Opus as his gut guess for the second killer, and Opus claimed to be the doctor and said he had saved Haiku. Opus was voted out 5 to 1, and in his last words he named Luna as the doctor, but Terra was the doctor, and the town won.
